title: Digital health literacy and the independent use of (AI-powered) digital applications by cancer patients
summary:
The planned study examines how well cancer patients can navigate digital health information—particularly new AI-based applications.
What is it about? (Background): 
Many patients feel they are not sufficiently informed about their condition. At the same time, digital resources, such as websites or AI tools, are becoming increasingly important. The study aims to determine whether and how patients use, understand, and trust these resources.
What exactly is being investigated? (Research question): 
How frequently cancer patients use digital and AI-supported applications; how well they can handle digital health information (digital health literacy); how high their trust in and acceptance of such technologies is; what experiences, expectations, opportunities, and risks they perceive in them; and whether factors such as age, education, or type of illness play a role
How is the study conducted? (Methodology):
Participating patients complete a one-time questionnaire (approx. 15–20 minutes).
Some of them will also be invited to a personal interview (approx. 45–60 minutes) to describe their experiences in more detail.
Who can participate?
Adult women with breast or gynecological cancers who are being treated at specialized cancer centers and speak sufficient German.
Objective of the Study
The findings are intended to help better tailor digital services—particularly AI applications—to the needs of female cancer patients. The goal is to make these services more understandable, trustworthy, and helpful in making decisions throughout the course of the disease.
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of female genital organs

interventions.name: Women with gynaecological cancer (including breast cancer) complete a questionnaire on a one-off basis; a subgroup of these women take part in a one-off interview.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Capacity to consent 
• Confirmed cancer diagnosis (ICD-10: C50, C51–C58) 
• Treatment at a breast or gynecologic cancer center within the CIO ABCD network
Exclusion criteria:
• Inability to complete questionnaires 
• Insufficient knowledge of the German language 
• For qualitative interviews only: Inability to conduct in-person interviews (e.g., deafness)
